$comment: THE SPEC. Written at definition, read by tools/board.mjs.
One thing here is a rule: the ratchet. A member may never score below its own best.
Everything else is a reading. Gauges report; they do not stop the loop.
Delete these $comment keys once you have filled it in.
definingFeature: {{the one thing that makes this THIS. It exists in round one, however crudely. A forest game with no trees at hour ten was building something else.}}

build.$comment: How the product is built, as a command that exits 0. doctor.mjs runs this when it finds an interrupted run: a process killed mid-edit leaves source that no longer parses, and an hour spent measuring a broken build looks exactly like an hour of work.
build.command: {{e.g. node tools/bundle.mjs — must exit non-zero if the product will not build}}

capture.$comment: What a frame costs. Iterate at working resolution; full is for frames you keep. Captures serialize — on a software rasterizer, parallel captures are SLOWER than serial ones, and the timings blame resolution for what is contention.

reference.$comment: The bar. Frozen so it cannot move between rounds. artifact > sourced > model-prior.
reference.target: {{the named target, e.g. 'a shipped AAA first-person shooter, lit and surfaced to that standard'}}

primaryMember: {{the ONE member Act I takes to the notch — pick the shot the concept is sold on}}

fidelity.$comment: The climb. This is what every round must move.

scale.$comment: Calibrate what the numbers MEAN before scoring anything. 0-100 not 1-10: a round that genuinely improves the build often moves a 10-point scale by zero, which reads as a stall that isn't one. Adapt the wording; do not invent a ladder from nothing.
scale.90: indistinguishable from the reference in a blind A/B
scale.76: clearly professional — would pass as a small-studio release
scale.60: a good indie build; clearly not the reference, and a trained eye says why immediately

gauges.$comment: Advisory. Reported every round, never blocking. A gauge earns its keep by changing what you do next.

coverage.$comment: Act II only. Width tracks quality — 1 member, then a handful, then this.

player.$comment: Built in Act II. Denials are asserted at runtime; the handicap is verified.
player.success: {{what counts as succeeding, as a predicate a program can check}}

anchors.$comment: Drift detection, once scores have been climbing a while.

coupled.$comment: Subsystems that are secretly one system and must be worked by one owner at a time. Parallel agents there break each other's assumptions while all of them report success.
coupled.why: {{what mutual dependency makes parallel work fail here}}

notes.$comment: What the instrument cannot see. Be honest here rather than implying full coverage.
